collection.description: After a harmless village game goes wrong, everyone blames a teenager, but a small child saw what happened.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: After a harmless village game goes wrong, everyone blames (teen), but (child), a small child, saw what happened.

choices.label: Let the Child Explain Without Coaching
Ask the Teen to Tell Their Side

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: (child) describes a loose game marker that caused the confusion.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: (child) admits they saw only part of the event, and the adults avoid overstating the account.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: (teen) explains their actions and is finally heard.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: (teen) acknowledges a mistake but disputes the unfair accusation.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: A worn cord explains the unexpected result.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The equipment is sound, so the group examines the game rules instead.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: Adults apologize for assuming (teen) was careless.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (child) learns that being believed includes being allowed to say they are unsure.
